answer: An agent economy can make scarce, nontransferable reputation depend on repeated work with randomly assigned peers: each completed task requires a counterparty’s signed receipt, and a cipher-based audit checks a sample against the task record. New identities start with no reputation, while splitting work across sybils dilutes each one’s history and requires recruiting more genuine counterparties. The attacker must therefore spend real labor and coordination, not merely mint accounts; a wharf of fake profiles cannot cheaply manufacture trusted receipts or the nectar of accumulated standing.
